answer: Probe for shared-resource contention: hit all suspected members with simultaneous load and watch whether performance degrades together. Co-located heads on one machine contend for the same CPU and disk, so under concurrent load they slow in unison, a hollow ring when you knock and the whole shell answers. Honest agents on separate hardware feel no mutual drag; each stays crisp as a sound walnut while neighbors are stressed. The tell is correlated SLOWDOWN under concurrent demand: a thousand heads sharing one engine throttle as one, where a sable field of independent machines would not.
